question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

You will certain pay for what you have done to your mother.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the omission of the adverb "**certainly**" after the verb "**will**."
 
• Adverbs are used to modify verbs and should be correctly placed for grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**You will certainly**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"You **will certainly** pay for what you have done to your mother."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "done to your mother." **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 2: "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 4.
 
• **Option 3: "pay for what you have"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "You will certain"** – This part of the sentence contains the error of missing the adverb **"certainly."**
